name: Dattātreya
summary: Son of Atri and Anasūyā, regarded as a form of Viṣṇu (or of the trimūrti) who 'gave himself' (datta) to Atri; in the minor Upaniṣads he teaches Sāṅkṛti the eightfold yoga (Darśana) and the nature of the avadhūta (Avadhūta), is named among the paramahaṃsas who live with unmanifest marks (Jābāla 6, Bhikṣuka, Nāradaparivrājaka 3.86), and is the 'most manifest' form of Brahman in Śāṇḍilya 3.

name: Sāṅkṛti
summary: Sage who questions Dattātreya in the Darśana and Avadhūta Upaniṣads and visits the sun's world in the Akṣi Upaniṣad; at the end of the Darśana he abides fearless in the Self.

name: Ṛbhu
summary: Sage of the Advaita dialogues: taught by Varāha after long austerity (Varāha 1–3), he teaches his disciple Nidāgha (Varāha 4–5, Tejobindu 5, Mahā, Annapūrṇā); named among the paramahaṃsas (Jābāla 6, Nāradaparivrājaka 3.86).

name: Nidāgha
summary: Disciple of Ṛbhu in the Varāha, Tejobindu, Mahā and Annapūrṇā Upaniṣads; asks about the seven stages (bhūmikā) and about yoga; named among the paramahaṃsas and among rudrākṣa-wearing sages.

name: Varāha (the Boar avatāra)
summary: Viṣṇu's boar form, who appears to Ṛbhu after twelve divine years of austerity and teaches him the 96 tattvas and non-dual knowledge (Varāha 1–3).

name: Śiva (as teacher)
summary: Śiva/Maheśvara as speaker: teaches Brahmā the Yogaśikhā and Yogakuṇḍalī ch.3, teaches Kumāra in the Tejobindu, Maitreya in the Maitreya, Śuka in the Śukarahasya, and Pārvatī the haṃsa-vidyā reported in the Haṃsa; whispers the tāraka to the dying at Kāśī (Muktikā 1.19–21, Jābāla 1).

name: Nārāyaṇa / Ādi-Nārāyaṇa (as teacher)
summary: Viṣṇu as speaker: the Person in the solar orb who teaches Yājñavalkya (Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇa), Ādi-Nārāyaṇa who answers Brahmā on the paramahaṃsa and the avadhūta (Paramahaṃsaparivrājaka, Turīyātīta), Mahāviṣṇu of the Tripādvibhūti, and Hṛṣīkeśa who teaches Brahmā the Yogatattva.

name: Rāma (as teacher)
summary: Rāma, regarded as the supreme Brahman, teaches Hanumān the canon of 108 Upaniṣads and the path to liberation in the Muktikā; the Rāma-Upaniṣads and Upaniṣad Brahmayogin's maṅgala verses make him the goal of every Upaniṣad.

name: Hanumān
summary: Rāma's devotee, the questioner of the Muktikā; in the Rāmarahasya he teaches Sanaka, Prahlāda and others that Rāma is the supreme Brahman.

name: Kālāgnirudra
summary: Rudra as 'fire of time': teaches Sanatkumāra the tripuṇḍra (Kālāgnirudra) and Bhusuṇḍa the sacred ash (Bṛhajjābāla); rudrākṣa beads arise from his tears (Rudrākṣajābāla).

name: Āditya (the Sun as teacher)
summary: The Sun-god who instructs visitors to his world: Triśikhi (Triśikhibrāhmaṇa), Sāṅkṛti (Akṣi); in the Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇa Yājñavalkya goes to the solar world and is taught by the Person there (Nārāyaṇa).

name: Skanda / Guha
summary: Son of Śiva: teaches Prajāpati the rosary (Akṣamālikā); the Skanda Upaniṣad is his declaration of the identity of jīva and Śiva; in the Jābāli his line (Īśāna → Ṣaḍānana → Jābāli) transmits the Paśupati teaching.

name: Sanatsujāta
summary: One of Brahmā's mind-born sons; in this recension of the Haṃsa Upaniṣad he teaches Gautama the haṃsa-vidyā that Śiva told Pārvatī.

name: Gautama (questioner of the Haṃsa)
summary: Sage who asks for the means to brahmavidyā in the Haṃsa Upaniṣad; Brahmavidyā 53 also addresses a Gautama. Identity with other Gautamas not asserted.

name: Mārkaṇḍeya
summary: Long-lived sage whom Śaunaka and others ask, in the Dakṣiṇāmūrti Upaniṣad, how he lives in bliss; he answers with the knowledge of Śiva as Dakṣiṇāmūrti.

name: Śuka
summary: Son of Vyāsa: receives the great sayings from Śiva at his initiation (Śukarahasya), asks about Rudra (Rudrahṛdaya); model of the 'bird's path' of immediate liberation (Varāha 4.34–37) and named among paramahaṃsas (Bhikṣuka, Yājñavalkya).

name: Atri
summary: Vedic seer who questions Yājñavalkya about Avimukta and the sacred thread (Jābāla 2, 5; Yājñavalkya Upaniṣad); father of Dattātreya.

name: Bṛhaspati
summary: Preceptor of the gods who asks Yājñavalkya about Kurukṣetra/Avimukta (Jābāla 1; Rāmottaratāpanī).

name: Bharadvāja
summary: Vedic seer who asks Yājñavalkya about the tāraka (Rāmottaratāpanī; Tārasāra) and is among the rudrākṣa-wearing sages (Rudrākṣajābāla); named among the kuṭīcaka renouncers (Bhikṣuka).

name: Maitreya
summary: Sage who goes to Kailāsa and is taught by Mahādeva that the body is a temple and the jīva is Śiva (Maitreya Upaniṣad 2). Distinct from Yājñavalkya's wife Maitreyī.

name: Triśikhi
summary: A brāhmaṇa who goes to Āditya's world with questions on body, self and liberation (Triśikhibrāhmaṇa).

name: Paiṅgala
summary: Disciple who serves Yājñavalkya for twelve years and then asks about kaivalya (Paiṅgala Upaniṣad).

name: Saṃvartaka
summary: Named first among the paramahaṃsas who live with unmanifest marks and conduct (Jābāla 6; Bhikṣuka; Nāradaparivrājaka 3.86).

name: Durvāsas
summary: Irascible sage named among the paramahaṃsas (Jābāla 6; Nāradaparivrājaka 3.86); in the Gopālottaratāpanī he teaches the gopīs.

name: Jaḍabharata
summary: The 'dull' Bharata who hid his knowledge; named among the paramahaṃsas (Jābāla 6; Bhikṣuka) and among rudrākṣa-wearers.

name: Raivataka
summary: Named among the paramahaṃsas (Jābāla 6; Nāradaparivrājaka 3.86).

name: Hārītaka
summary: Named among the paramahaṃsas in the Bhikṣuka and Yājñavalkya Upaniṣads.

name: Vaiśravaṇa (Vālakhilya)
summary: Questioner in the Pāśupatabrahma Upaniṣad, called a son of Brahmā and a Vālakhilya; not the Kubera of the Purāṇas as far as the text says.

name: Jābāli
summary: Teacher of the Jābāli Upaniṣad, who received the Paśupati teaching through Īśāna and Ṣaḍānana and teaches Paippalādi the meaning of paśu and Paśupati.

name: Paippalādi
summary: Questioner of Jābāli in the Jābāli Upaniṣad (a descendant or pupil of Pippalāda by name).

name: Bhusuṇḍa (Jābāla)
summary: Questioner in the Bṛhajjābāla (of Kālāgnirudra) and Bhasmajābāla (of Mahādeva) on sacred ash.

name: Āśvalāyana
summary: Ṛgvedic sage who approaches Parameṣṭhin for brahmavidyā (Kaivalya 1.1) and who teaches the sages the Sarasvatī-vidyā (Sarasvatīrahasya). Identity with the Kausalya Āśvalāyana of the Praśna not asserted.

name: Upaniṣad Brahmayogin
summary: Advaitin renouncer of Kāñcīpuram who wrote commentaries on all 108 Muktikā Upaniṣads; his maṅgala verses open each text in the South Indian printed collection used here.

name: Nārāyaṇa (author of Dīpikās)
summary: Commentator who glossed many Atharvan and minor Upaniṣads (e.g. the Nīlarudra); dates uncertain.

name: Śaṅkarānanda
summary: Advaitin commentator (Dīpikās) on many Upaniṣads including Atharvan ones; tradition makes him a teacher of Vidyāraṇya.

name: Yādavaprakāśa
summary: Bhedābheda Vedāntin, remembered in Śrīvaiṣṇava tradition as Rāmānuja's first teacher, later a tridaṇḍin renouncer; author of the Yatidharmasamuccaya on renouncers' rules.

name: Vāsudevāśrama
summary: Author of the Yatidharmaprakāśa, a digest of the renouncer's rules.

name: Dārā Shikoh
summary: Mughal prince (1615–1659) who with pandits translated some fifty Upaniṣads into Persian (Sirr-i Akbar, 1657).

name: Yājñavalkya
summary: U04 contribution: in the minor Upaniṣads Yājñavalkya teaches Bṛhaspati, Atri and Janaka on Avimukta, the tāraka and renunciation 'on the very day one becomes dispassionate' (Jābāla, Yājñavalkya Upaniṣad), is taught by the Person in the sun (Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇa), teaches Paiṅgala, and is named among the kuṭīcaka renouncers (Bhikṣuka).

name: Janaka of Videha
summary: U04 contribution: asks Yājñavalkya about renunciation (Jābāla 4; Yājñavalkya Upaniṣad); in the Mahā Upaniṣad he teaches Śuka.

name: Nārada
summary: U04 contribution: asks the Lord about the paramahaṃsa (Paramahaṃsa), Brahmā about crossing Kali (Kalisantaraṇa), Vāsudeva about the ūrdhvapuṇḍra (Vāsudeva) and Brahmā about Hayagrīva; teaches the sages at Naimiṣa the renouncer's life (Nāradaparivrājaka).

name: Sanatkumāra
summary: U04 contribution: asks Kālāgnirudra about the tripuṇḍra (Kālāgnirudra) and, with Pippalāda and Aṅgiras, asks Atharvan about the first meditation (Atharvaśikhā).

name: Atharvan
summary: U04 contribution: teaches Śāṇḍilya the eight-limbed yoga and brahmavidyā (Śāṇḍilya) and teaches Pippalāda, Aṅgiras and Sanatkumāra the meditation on Oṃ (Atharvaśikhā); speaker of the short Mahā Upaniṣad.

name: Śāṇḍilya
summary: U04 contribution: disciple of Atharvan in the Śāṇḍilya Upaniṣad, who, not finding brahmavidyā in the four Vedas, asks for it.

name: Pippalāda
summary: U04 contribution: answers Śaunaka in the Brahma and Parabrahma Upaniṣads (prāṇa as self; inner topknot and thread); as Paippalāda asks the Lord in the Pañcabrahma and Brahmā in the Śarabha.

name: Śaunaka Mahāśāla
summary: U04 contribution: asks Pippalāda in the Brahma and Parabrahma Upaniṣads; leads the sages who ask Mārkaṇḍeya (Dakṣiṇāmūrti) and hear Nārada at Naimiṣa (Nāradaparivrājaka).

name: Brahmā
summary: U04 contribution: answers Nārada (Kalisantaraṇa, Nāradaparivrājaka 2), Vaiśravaṇa (Pāśupatabrahma), Paippalāda (Śarabha); taught by Viṣṇu (Yogatattva) and Śiva (Yogaśikhā); as Parameṣṭhin teaches Āśvalāyana (Kaivalya).

name: Prajāpati
summary: U04 contribution: teaches Āruṇi renunciation (Āruṇi), the gods on Sītā (Sītā) and renunciation (Kaṭharudra), and sees the Narasiṃha mantra-king (Nṛsiṃhatāpanī).

name: Uddālaka Āruṇi
summary: U04 contribution: tradition identifies him with the Āruṇi who goes to Prajāpati's world to learn renunciation (Āruṇi Upaniṣad); named among paramahaṃsas (Jābāla 6; Bhikṣuka).

name: Śvetaketu
summary: U04 contribution: named among the paramahaṃsas (Jābāla 6; Bhikṣuka; Nāradaparivrājaka 3.86).

name: Vāmadeva
summary: U04 contribution: model of the 'ant's path' of gradual liberation through births (Varāha 4.38–42) and named among the paramahaṃsas (Bhikṣuka).

name: Śākāyanya
summary: U04 contribution: his teaching to Bṛhadratha is recapitulated in Maitreya Upaniṣad 1.

name: Raikva
summary: U04 contribution: asks the questions answered in the Subāla Upaniṣad (in some sections).

name: Vyāsa
summary: U04 contribution: asks Śiva to instruct Śuka (Śukarahasya) and answers Śuka on Rudra (Rudrahṛdaya).

name: Śaṅkara
summary: U04 contribution: cites the Jābāla (4) for renunciation directly from studentship (Brahmasūtrabhāṣya 3.4.20); a commentary on the Nṛsiṃhatāpanī is attributed to him (questioned by scholars). The Daśanāmī tradition traces its four maṭhas to him (Maṭhāmnāya).

name: Vidyāraṇya
summary: U04 contribution: the Jīvanmuktiviveka builds its account of the knower's renunciation and liberation while living on the Saṃnyāsa Upaniṣads and the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha.

name: Bhāskararāya
summary: U04 contribution: commented on the Tripurā, Bhāvanā and Kaula Upaniṣads.
